invalid_if: Safeguards fall below the minimum set out in Rule 6 of the DPDP Rules, 2025
Logs are retained for less than one year without a lawful basis
name: Reasonable Security Safeguards
title: Security Safeguards
text:
The Processor shall take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach, as Section 8(5) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires. Those safeguards shall include, at a minimum, the measures below, which are those prescribed by Rule 6 of the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025. The Parties adopt them by contract with effect from the date of this Agreement, and record that Rule 6 itself comes into force on 14 May 2027.
(a) Appropriate protection of personal data by encryption, obfuscation, masking, or the use of virtual tokens.
(b) Control over access to the computer resources on which personal data is processed.
(c) Visibility over who accesses personal data, through logs, monitoring, and review, so that an unauthorised access can be detected, investigated, and remedied.
(d) Retention of those logs and of the personal data for a period of one year, unless a longer period is required by law, so that an unauthorised access may be traced.
(e) Measures for the continued processing of personal data in the event of loss of access, including reasonable backups.
(f) Appropriate provision in every contract the Processor enters into with any person it engages, requiring that person to take the same safeguards.
The Processor shall keep these safeguards under review and shall not reduce them during the term of this Agreement.

legal_basis.note: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control by taking reasonable security safeguards
Reasonable security safeguards: encryption or masking or tokens, access control, logs and monitoring, retention of logs for one year, backups, and contractual flow-down

source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
statutory_reference: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 - R.6
authoring_note:
The limbs track Rule 6 rather than paraphrasing it, because the penalty for failing to take reasonable security safeguards is the largest in the Act's Schedule and a general 'industry standard measures' formula gives the Fiduciary nothing to audit against. The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 14 November 2025 with a phased commencement (Rule 1): Rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21 on publication; Rule 4 on 14 November 2026; and Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 on 14 May 2027. This clause is drafted to the Rules as notified, so the contract is compliant ahead of the date rather than needing renegotiation on it. The advocate should decide whether to state the commencement dates in the document itself.

COMMENCEMENT. The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 14 November 2025 with a phased commencement under Rule 1: Rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21 on publication; Rule 4 on 14 November 2026; and Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 on 14 May 2027. This clause previously stated the Rule as a presently binding legal obligation, which it is not yet. It now states the Act obligation as the operative source, adopts the Rule's content BY CONTRACT from the date of the agreement, and records the Rule's own commencement date. That keeps the contract compliant ahead of the date without asserting a state of the law that is untrue. A reviewing advocate flagged the original wording, and was right to.
